description: Conformance corpus for standards/090-web-client.md. 'validity': the value must validate (or fail) against the named schema root — 'runtime-config' or 'error-report'. 'behaviour': black-box cases a live client and its serving process must satisfy; the harness drives the stimulus and asserts 'expect'. An implementation passes the whole file or names the case it fails. The runtime-config cases are at schema version 3: field names say what each field is, surface_class tells one contract which estate surface it serves (091 WE1), and the document is fetched from /config.json.

validity.note: the whole document a product client needs: which surface and environment it is, where the API is, and how to start and end a session (WC1, WC2, 091 WE1)
the same bundle, same commit, different environment — which is the WC2 property the whole rule exists for; the flags are the anonymous global subset of 038 FF7, named as flags are

a front door has no session and no API, so it carries neither api_origin nor a login path; what it does carry is the per-environment values its pages need, under keys its own repository declares (091 WE3, WE4)
an internal surface is shaped like a product surface: it has a session and an API. What differs is the identity provider behind login_path, which this document does not name (091 WE1)
a product client cannot ask the API where the API is; the conditional requirement is the ordering problem WC2 exists to solve
a front door that is told where an API is has been given the means to call one; 091 WE3 says it calls no authenticated API, and the schema holds the shape of that
the closed property set is the enforcement of 'nothing secret goes here' — this document is served to every anonymous visitor (WC2)

the browser is not an OAuth participant, so it is told where to navigate and nothing about the provider. The closed set is what keeps a client_id or issuer from arriving here and inviting the page to do an exchange itself (WC1)

the correction that produced schemaVersion 2 and still holds at 3: a serving origin cannot know which frontend build the browser is running, so provenance is compiled into the bundle and never served (WC2)

the version 2 names are gone, not aliased: api_base_url was always an origin and the auth wrapper named nothing. No implementation consumed version 2, so the deprecation window is nil and the old shape is simply invalid (PC6)
a login path resolved against the current route sends the user somewhere different depending on where they were when the session expired
an origin is scheme, host and port; the version prefix is 050 HA5's and belongs to the generated client (WC3), not to a value the serving host renders

a nested object here is application configuration wearing a bootstrap's name; the bootstrap carries scalars the serving origin's environment can render, and anything with structure belongs on /api/config (WC2)

validity.note: the conditional requirement: an api_error without the server's request id cannot be joined to anything, which is the whole correlation mechanism WC5 relies on

validity.note: browsers hold stale bundles longer than servers hold stale builds; a trace against unknown source is unreadable (WC5)

validity.note: the closed property set is what stops a reporter shipping the user's form to a third party. This is the case the shape exists for (WC5)

validity.note: presentation is for the viewer, never for the wire — the client formats for display and still sends the base form (WC4, IP4)

behaviour.stimulus: grep the built bundle for the api_origin of any environment, and for any value of surface_settings
behaviour.note: the WC2 gate, and the cheapest in this standard: one artifact promoted through environments, so the value cannot be in it

behaviour.stimulus: serve the identical build output from a staging server and a production server

expect.each_client: fetches /config.json naming its own environment and api_origin

behaviour.note: the property WC2 is actually protecting; a build-time bake fails here and nowhere else

behaviour.stimulus: GET /config.json from the origin that served the bundle, twice, with a deployment between that changes one surface_settings value
behaviour.note: the path is pinned so every surface, a CDN-hosted front door included, is bootstrapped the same way; no-store is what lets a deployment change a value without a rebuild or a cache purge (WC2)

behaviour.stimulus: complete a login, then read localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB
behaviour.note: WC1's observable half. The browser is never given a token, so there is nothing to store; this catches a client that started holding one without saying so

behaviour.stimulus: make a mutating call that fails with 503, and let the client retry
behaviour.note: a fresh key on the retry defeats the mechanism entirely and duplicates the charge (WC3, HA6)
the exponent belongs to the currency; dividing by 100 is wrong for JPY and for every three-exponent currency (WC4, IP5)

behaviour.stimulus: render the instant 2026-01-01T03:00:00.000Z as a date, with the viewer's zone set to America/Los_Angeles
behaviour.note: the calendar day an instant falls on depends on the zone; rendering the UTC date directly is off by one for a predictable fraction of users every day (WC4)
